description:
Build a hedonic pricing model for San Francisco buildings using UrbanSim.

Task: Using Jupyter Lab and the UrbanSim framework, create a hedonic regression model that predicts residential building sale prices based on building characteristics.

REQUIREMENTS:
- Open the Jupyter notebook at /home/ga/urbansim_projects/notebooks/hedonic_model.ipynb
- Load the San Francisco buildings data from /home/ga/urbansim_projects/data/sanfran_public.h5
- Use the 'buildings' table which contains columns like residential_sales_price, building_sqft, year_built, stories, residential_units, and non_residential_sqft
- Note: residential_sales_price values are synthetically generated from census data, so model fit may vary
- Build an OLS regression model predicting residential_sales_price from at least 3 building features (e.g., building_sqft, year_built, stories)
- Handle missing values appropriately (drop NaN rows)
- Print the regression summary showing R-squared and coefficients
- Save the model coefficients to a CSV file at /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/hedonic_coefficients.csv with columns: variable, coefficient, std_error, p_value
- Save a scatter plot of predicted vs actual prices to /home/ga/urbansim_projects/output/hedonic_scatter.png

The notebook should be executed with all cells run and outputs visible.
